title: Space Tech Briefing — October 03, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts, and welcome to your daily dose of the cosmos! It's Friday, October 03, 2026, and the universe is buzzing with incredible advancements and opportunities. Let's dive right in!

First up, as we look back at some major recent developments, a fantastic initiative from the French space agency, CNES, has been making waves. Their teams have been actively visiting universities and major schools. This isn't just a casual visit; they're presenting the diverse career paths available within CNES and answering all your burning questions about working in the space industry. It's a brilliant move to inspire the next generation of engineers, scientists, and innovators to join the exciting world of space. If CNES is coming to your institution, make sure you don't miss out on this incredible opportunity!

And speaking of incredible opportunities and milestones, let's recap a truly historic moment that happened just this Monday, September 28th. SpaceX's Starship achieved its first-ever orbital flight! This was a monumental leap forward for the ambitious spacecraft. The mission saw a Super Heavy Block 3, designated Booster 21, paired with Starship Ship 41, the V3 version. The primary goal of this 14th flight was to place Starship into a low Earth orbit, specifically around 275 kilometers high, for approximately six revolutions over about ten hours. But that wasn't all; the mission aimed to test the entire flight sequence. This included a successful stage separation, the controlled return and splashdown of the Super Heavy booster in the Gulf of Mexico, followed by the Ship's deorbit, atmospheric re-entry, and a planned splashdown in the Pacific, west of Chile. It's important to note that tower recovery for both stages was not part of this particular flight plan. What an achievement, truly pushing the boundaries of spaceflight!

And that's your morning briefing from the final frontier! Thank you for joining us today. Stay curious, keep looking up, and we'll connect again soon for more cosmic updates. Have a stellar day!
